rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ‘they said’ refers to the polytheists who objected to the Qur’an’s gradual descent.
rows.anchor: وضمير { وقال } ظاهر في أنه عائد إلى المشركين

words: لَوْلَا نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ جُمْلَةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ
rows.speaker: المشركون
rows.claim: The polytheists argued that, if the Qur’an came from God, it would have been revealed all at once.
rows.anchor: المشركون نسوا ذلك أو جهلوا فقالوا : هلا نزل القرآن على محمد جملة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier scriptures were also revealed in portions: the Torah’s ten commandments, the Gospel as Jesus’s spoken sayings, and the Psalms in many parts; none was a complete book at once.
rows.anchor: جملة واحدة وإنما كانت وحيا مفرقا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative report says Jews or Christians made the objection.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن قائل هذا اليهود أو النصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Jews or Christians said this, it was slander, since they knew their own Torah, Gospel, and Psalms were revealed piecemeal.
rows.anchor: لأنهم يعلمون أنه لم تنزل التوراة والإنجيل والزبور إلا مفرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He dismisses commentators’ effort to explain the difference by contrasting Muhammad’s illiteracy with earlier prophets: none of their books descended as a complete volume.
rows.anchor: فإن تلك الكتب لم تنزل أسفارا تامة قط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here نزل means أنزل and, given ‘all at once,’ does not signal the intensive or repeated sense of the verb form.
rows.anchor: و { نزل } هنا مرادف أنزل وليس فيه إيذان بما يدل عليه التفعيل من التكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response turns from the objectors to the Prophet, explaining the wisdom of gradual revelation and expressing God’s favor in strengthening and easing matters for him.
rows.anchor: فهو كلام مستأنف فيه رد لما أرادوه من قولهم : { لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كَذَٰلِكَ answers the demand for one-time revelation and points back to the gradual mode implied in their hypothetical; it stands as an accusative substitute for an absolute object, estimated as ‘We revealed it thus.’
rows.anchor: فاسم الإشارة في محل نصب على أنه نائب عن مفعول مطلق جاء بدلا عن الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase functions as a fresh turn in the dialogue, answering the objection by naming the very gradual revelation whose wisdom they missed.
rows.anchor: فالتقدير : أنزلناه إنزالا كذلك الإنزال المنجم .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose lām in لِنُثَبِّتَ attaches to the implicit verb indicated by كَذَٰلِكَ.
rows.anchor: واللام في { لنثبت } متعلقة بالفعل المقدر الذي دل عليه { كذلك } .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tathbīt means making something firm; firmness is stability in place without wavering, and it is also figuratively certainty and assurance of good.
rows.anchor: والتثبيت : جعل الشيء ثابتا . والثبات : استقرار الشيء في مكانه غير متزلزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here fuʾād means the intellect; gradual revelation makes it steady in the Qur’an’s words and meanings, without confusion.
rows.anchor: والفؤاد : هنا العقل . وتثبيته بذلك الإنزال جعله ثابتا في ألفاظه ومعانيه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says revelation came in portions to strengthen the Prophet’s heart so he could understand and memorize it, since learners retain knowledge better when it comes successively.
rows.anchor: فمنه ما قاله الزمخشري : الحكمة في تفريقه أن نقوي بتفريقه فؤادك حتى تعيه وتحفظه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also says revelation matched occasions, events, and questioners’ answers, making its audience more receptive and active, which reassured the Prophet and expanded his heart.
rows.anchor: أنه كان ينزل على حسب الدواعي والحوادث وجوابات السائلين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī argues that challenging opponents with portions as each arrived made the miracle clearer and the proof stronger than one complete descent.
rows.anchor: إن تنزيله مفرقا وتحديهم بأن يأتوا ببعض تلك التفارق كلما نزل شيء منها

rows.speaker: الجد الوزير
rows.claim: The author’s grandfather, the vizier, says gradual descent allows verses to match circumstances and suit their setting, completing their miraculous quality.
rows.anchor: ومنه ما قاله الجد الوزير رحمه الله : إن القرآن لو لم ينزل منجما على حسب الحوادث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author adds that gradual revelation helps memorizers understand and reflect on the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وقلت : إن نزوله منجما أعون لحفاظه على فهمه وتدبره .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وَرَتَّلْنَٰهُ is coordinated with كَذَٰلِكَ: God revealed it in portions and arranged it with measured order.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { ورتلناه ترتيلا } عطف على قوله { كذلك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tartīl describes speech whose indications are well composed; the language authorities derive it from teeth spaced like chamomile blossoms, though they cite no Arabic poetic evidence.
rows.anchor: واتفقت أقوال أيمة اللغة على أن هذا الترتيل مأخوذ من قولهم : ثغر مرتل ورتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tartīl may describe revelation: it arrived over time, yet each completed sūra has ordered, coherent verses, clearly articulated rather than accumulated; such coherence across time signals divine origin.
rows.anchor: فإذا كمل إنزال سورة جاءت آياتها مرتبة متناسبة كأنها أنزلت جملة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ‘We arranged it’ means God commanded measured recitation, with no haste and with every letter and vowel articulated clearly, as in al-Muzzammil.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد ب { رتلناه } أمرنا بترتيله ، أي بقراءته مرتلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تَرْتِيلًۭا is an accusative cognate object; its indefiniteness conveys grandeur and specifies the kind of measured arrangement.
rows.anchor: و { ترتيلا } مصدر منصوب على المفعول المطلق قصد به ما في التنكير من معنى التعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse sequence likens the Qur’an’s gradual revelation to the shadow’s gradual extension, which God could have left still.
rows.anchor: أفاد تمثيل هيئة تنزيل القرآن منجما بهيئة مد الظل مدرجا ولو شاء لجعله ساكنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Read literally, the arrangement teaches about the fine details of God’s power in extending and contracting the shadow; Ibn ʿĀshūr treats this as using the wording in its literal and figurative senses.
rows.anchor: العبرة بمد الظل وقبضه في إثبات دقائق قدرة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metaphor makes guidance like sunlight and the shrinking of unbelief’s darkness like a long shadow contracting after sunrise; this explains the link to the day’s resurrection.
rows.anchor: وبهذه النكتة عطف قوله { ثم قبضناه إلينا قبضا يسيرا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The confirmatory question accommodates inattentive listeners, deniers, and the rightly guided: it prompts the first to reflect, reproves the second, and urges the third to look further.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام تقريري فهو صالح لطبقات السامعين : من غافل يسأل عن غفلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing is visual, but the verb also carries the sense of looking, so it takes إِلَىٰ before its object.
rows.anchor: والرؤية بصرية ، وقد ضمن الفعل معنى النظر فعدي إلى المرئي بحرف ( إلى ) .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Madd means to spread out something contracted or interwoven, as a rope or hand; commonly figurative for increase, it means an increase in the shadow’s extent here.
rows.anchor: والمد : بسط الشيء المنقبض المتداخل يقال : مد الحبل ومد يده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the intended object of seeing is a state, the verb can take ‘how’ directly; when attention is on an entity, it takes that entity first and then its state by a circumstantial phrase or clause.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين التعديتين أن الأولى يقصد منها العناية بالحالة لا بصاحبها

words: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَيْفَ مَدَّ ٱلظِّلَّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because this passage establishes God’s exclusive divinity, it first names the entity and then gives the state, like an appositional complement; the emphasis falls on God as possessor of the act.
rows.anchor: أوثر تعلق فعل الرؤية باسم الذات ابتداء ثم مجيء الحال بعد ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier writings are the books of earlier prophets, including the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and other scriptures known collectively.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { في زبر الأولين } أي كتب الرسل السالفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun cannot mean the Qur’an’s revealed wording, since its sūras and verses are not written verbatim in earlier scriptures; it refers instead to its name, distinctive description, or meanings.
rows.anchor: إذ ليست سور القرآن وآياته مسطورة في زبر الأولين بلفظها كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the name-and-description reading, earlier books foretold Muhammad and a messenger who would bring a book, as in the Qur’an’s report that the unlettered Prophet is written in the Torah and Gospel.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى أن ذكر القرآن وارد في كتب الأولين ، أي جاءت بشارات بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Deuteronomy 18 Moses promises a prophet like himself from his brethren; Ibn ʿĀshūr identifies Israel’s brethren as Arabs, citing Ishmael’s descendants living opposite their brethren, and sees no other post-Mosaic prophet bringing comparable law.
rows.anchor: ففي سفر التثنية من كتب موسى عليه السلام في الإصحاح الثامن عشر قول موسى : ( قال لي الرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Deuteronomy promise that God will put His words in the prophet’s mouth refers to the Qur’an revealed to Muhammad, which he recites.
rows.anchor: وكلام الله المجعول في فمه هو القرآن الموحى به إليه وهو يتلوه

rows.speaker: عيسى عليه السلام
rows.claim: As quoted in Matthew 24, Jesus warns of many false prophets and says the enduring message will be preached throughout the inhabited world as testimony to all nations before the end.
rows.anchor: وفي إنجيل متى الإصحاح الرابع والعشرين قال عيسى عليه السلام : ( ويقوم أنبياء كذبة كثيرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr reads that universal proclamation as the revelation and Qur’an addressed to all peoples, linking it to the Qur’an’s statements about guiding humanity and setting out every kind of example.
rows.anchor: فالبشارة هي الوحي وهو القرآن وهو الكتاب الذي دعا جميع الأمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a third commendation of the Qur’an: Israelite scholars’ recognition is evidence supporting the preceding commendation, that earlier prophetic books attest to it.
rows.anchor: تنويه ثالث بالقرآن وحجة على التنويه الثاني به الذي هو شهادة كتب الأنبياء له بالصدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the clause is also a new commendation, it is coordinated with the preceding statement; if it served only as evidence, coordination would not be expected.
rows.anchor: فباعتبار كون هذه الجملة تنويها آخر بالقرآن عطفت على الجملة التي قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their knowing includes recognizing the Qur’an’s qualities and verifying that its bearer truly has those qualities, as well as knowing what it contains from their scriptures.
rows.anchor: وفعل : { يعلمه } شامل للعلم بصفة القرآن ، أي تحقق صدق الصفات الموصوف بها من جاء به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun may refer to the Qur’an, with the sense ‘know its mention,’ or to the previously stated fact that it is in earlier writings.
rows.anchor: وضمير { أن يعلمه } عائد إلى القرآن على تقدير : أن يعلم ذكره . ويجوز أن يعود على الحكم المذكور

rows.speaker: مصعب بن الزبير
rows.claim: At Iraq, Musʿab ibn al-Zubayr substituted recitation of the story’s opening for a speech on behalf of his brother: he gestured toward Syria for ʿAbd al-Malik, the Hijaz for ʿAbd Allāh and his supporters, and Iraq for al-Ḥajjāj.
rows.anchor: اكتفى مصعب بن الزبير بطالعها عن الخطبة التي حقه أن يخطب بها في الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 14 is an interlude within the story’s chronology, prompted by the promise to Moses’s mother; that promise was fulfilled when the narrative completed his return to her in verse 13.
rows.anchor: هذا اعتراض بين أجزاء القصة المرتبة على حسب ظهورها في الخارج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses received prophethood only after leaving Midian, as the later account says when he completed the term and set out with his family.
rows.anchor: وإنما أوتي الحكم أعني النبوءة بعد خروجه من أرض مدين كما سيجيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A parallel to this verse appears in Sūrat Yūsuf, though that verse lacks the additional description ‘and he became fully formed.’
rows.anchor: وتقدم نظير هذه الآية في سورة يوسف ، إلا قوله { واستوى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take istawā as a synonym of reaching full strength and therefore an emphasis; Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects this, taking ashudd as full strength and istiwāʾ as bodily completeness.
rows.anchor: و الحق أن الأشد كمال القوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istiwāʾ means bodily completeness, as when crops thicken and stand upright; Moses is described this way, unlike Joseph, because Moses was tall and fully built.
rows.anchor: وأن الاستواء : كمال البنية كقوله تعالى في وصف الزرع { فاستغلظ فاستوى على سوقه }

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic description says Moses was like one of the men of Shanūʾa; his full build helps explain why his blow killed the Egyptian.
rows.anchor: كما في الحديث ( كأنه من رجال شنؤة ) فكان كامل الأعضاء ولذلك كان وكزه القبطي قاضيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ḥukm means wisdom, while ʿilm means knowledge of God.
rows.anchor: والحكم : الحكمة ، والعلم : المعرفة بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’s migration resembles Abraham’s declaration that he was migrating to his Lord; God guided Moses toward Midian, where he would meet a prophet to teach him prophetic conduct, though Moses did not know his destination or whom he would meet.
rows.anchor: هذه هجرة نبوية تشبه هجرة إبراهيم عليه السلام إذ قال { إني مهاجر إلى ربي }

words: عَسَىٰ رَبِّىٓ أَن يَهْدِيَنِى سَوَآءَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about setting out toward Midian coordinates with omitted narrative: after leaving the city and wandering, Moses happened onto a road leading to Midian and prayed for guidance.
rows.anchor: فقوله تعالى { ولما توجه تلقاء مدين } عطف على جمل محذوفة إذ التقدير : ولما خرج من المدينة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Moses set out without knowing the road, relying only on good expectation of his Lord.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : خرج موسى ولا علم له بالطريق إلا حسن ظن بربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawajjaha means to turn one’s face, hence to set one’s course toward Midian.
rows.anchor: و { توجه } : ولى وجهه ، أي استقبل بسيره تلقاء مدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tilqāʾ is an uncommon verbal noun meaning meeting or proximity; it became a place adverb, here ‘toward the place facing Midian.’
rows.anchor: و { تلقاء } : أصله مصدر على وزن التفعال بكسر التاء ، وليس له نظير في كسر التاء إلا تمثال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Midian was a people descended from Midian, son of Abraham.
rows.anchor: و { مدين } : قوم من ذرية مدين بن إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Midian lay on the Red Sea’s western shore; from Rameses or Memphis Moses likely traveled southwest through Amalekite, Edomite, and Nabataean lands, about 850 miles or 45 days on foot, sleeping outdoors but staying on course.
rows.anchor: تلك مسافة ثمانمائة وخمسين ميلا تقريبا . وإذ قد كان موسى في سيره ذلك راجلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawāʾ is a straight, untwisted course; the prayer implicitly asks God to guide Moses into the true religion.
rows.anchor: والسواء : المستقيم النهج الذي لا التواء فيه . وقد ألهمه الله هذه الدعوة التي في طيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His arrival at Midian’s water means that he reached the land of Midian; warada here means arriving or reaching.
rows.anchor: يدل قوله { لما ورد ماء مدين } أنه بلغ أرض مدين ، وذلك حين ورد ماءهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Water’ means the watering place: tribes settled near water and used a tribe’s water-name as a name for its territory.
rows.anchor: وماء القوم هو الذي تعرف به ديارهم لأن القبائل كانت تقطن عند المياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A newcomer would head to the water because it gathered people, making it a natural place to find companions and a host.
rows.anchor: يناسب الغريب إذا جاء ديار قوم أن يقصد الماء لأنه مجتمع الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لَمَّا marks the time when one event occurs in relation to another: when Moses reached Midian, he found a group there.
rows.anchor: و { لما } حرف توقيت وجود شيء بوجود غيره ، أي عندما حل بأرض مدين وجد أمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ummah here means a large group.
rows.anchor: والأمة : الجماعة الكثيرة العدد ، وتقدم في قوله تعالى { كان الناس أمة واحدة }

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf, following Dalāʾil al-Iʿjāz, explains the omitted object of yasqūn as deliberately general—livestock or people—because the focus is the women’s withdrawal, not what was being watered.
rows.anchor: كما في ( الكشاف ) تبعا ( لدلائل الإعجاز ) ، فيكون من تنزيل الفعل المتعدي منزلة اللازم

rows.speaker: السكاكي
rows.claim: Al-Sakkākī, supported by his commentators al-Saʿd and al-Sayyid, instead treats the omitted object as an ellipsis for brevity.
rows.anchor: كما اختاره السكاكي وأيده شارحاه السعد والسيد

rows.speaker: الشيخان
rows.claim: For the omitted objects of ‘they hold back,’ ‘we give no water,’ and ‘he watered for them,’ Ibn ʿĀshūr says the two Shaykhs’ analysis is required; he finds no Qur’anic basis for the alternative elaboration by the author of al-Miftāḥ and his commentators, which depends on Israelite books to infer sheep.
rows.anchor: فيتعين فيها ما ذهب إليه الشيخان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min dūnihim means at a place farther from the crowd; dun originally describes what is lower, extended metaphorically to the direction reached after another place, as if walking down to it.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { من دونهم } في مكان غير المكان الذي حول الماء ، أي في جانب مباعد للأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun described by dūn is omitted through frequent use, leaving dūn to function like that missing noun.
rows.anchor: ويحذف الموصوف ب ( دون ) لكثرة الاستعمال فيصير ( دون ) بمنزلة ذلك الاسم المحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min with dūn can mark location, as in the Friday call, or mean ‘at’ according to Abū ʿUbayda’s usage; here it places the women away from the watering crowd.
rows.anchor: وحرف { من } مع ( دون ) يجوز أن يكون للظرفية مثل { إذا نودي للصلاة من يوم الجمعة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhawd literally drives livestock away from water; the word also figuratively applies to driving people away, as in the Prophetic report about people turned from his basin.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة الذود طرد الأنعام عن الماء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report speaks of people being driven away from the Prophet’s basin, an extended use of the verb for driving livestock from water.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله في الحديث ( فليذادن أقوام عن حوضي ) الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women were keeping their livestock from the water; given that Shuʿayb had sheep, the wording may be figurative or may use dhawḏ for all livestock, though lexicographers do not clearly settle its exact scope.
rows.anchor: وفي التوراة : أن شعيبا كان صاحب غنم وأن موسى رعى غنمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is a substitution explaining the circumstance of finding the two women apart from the crowd.
rows.anchor: وجملة { قال ما خطبكما } بدل اشتمال من جملة { ووجد من دونهم امرأتين تذودان }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khaṭb means an important matter or event; Moses asks about their story and why they came to the water but did not approach to water their flock.
rows.anchor: والخطب : الشأن والحدث المهم ، وتقدم عند قوله تعالى { قال ما خطبكن إذ راودتن يوسف عن نفسه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They avoid watering while the place is crowded and continue waiting until the shepherds depart; the imperfect verb presents their abstention as continuing until then.
rows.anchor: فأجابتا بأنهما كرهتا أن تسقيا في حين اكتظاظ المكان بالرعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-riʿāʾ is the plural of rāʿī, ‘shepherd.’
rows.anchor: و { الرعاء } : جمع راع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iṣdār means making the shepherds depart after watering, that is, sending them away with their animals so the crowd clears.
rows.anchor: والإصدار : الإرجاع عن السقي ، أي حتى يسقي الرعاء ويصدروا مواشيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their not pushing into the crowd reflects their good manners and fine upbringing.
rows.anchor: وصدهما عن المزاحمة عادتهما لأنهما كانتا ذواتي مروءة وتربية زكية

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read yuṣdir, with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on dāl, making it causative: the shepherds send their animals away from the water.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { يصدر } بضم الياء وكسر الدال

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, Abū ʿAmr, and Abū Jaʿfar read yaṣduru with fatḥa on the prefix and ḍamma on dāl, assigning the intransitive return from the water to the shepherds.
rows.anchor: وقرأه ابن عامر وأبو عمرو وأبو جعفر { يصدر } بفتح حرف المضارعة وضم الدال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second reading implies that the women water their animals every day, but the verse itself does not establish this as a daily habit.
rows.anchor: وهذا يقتضي أن تلك عادتهما كل يوم سقي ، وليس في اللفظ دلالة على أنه عادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their father’s age excuses their watering among men: they have no other man to draw water for them, and he is too weak to compete at the well.
rows.anchor: وكان قولهما { وأبونا شيخ كبير } اعتذارا عن حضورهما للسقي مع الرجال

rows.speaker: ابن العبري
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿIbrī says Jethro son of Reuel had seven daughters, two of whom went to water; he concludes that Jewish tradition identifies Shuʿayb as Jethro.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن العبري في ( تاريخه ) : يثرون بن رعويل له سبع بنات خرج للسقي منهما اثنتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exodus first calls their father Reuel and later Jethro, Moses’s father-in-law; Ibn ʿĀshūr regards these as names of the same man.
rows.anchor: وسماه في ذلك السفر أول مرة رعويل ثم أعاد الكلام عليه فسماه يثرون ووصفه بحمي موسى ، فالمسمى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling a prophet a priest reflects Jewish usage: a priest foretells the unseen and the term can denote a Jewish religious official.
rows.anchor: والتعبير عن النبي بالكاهن اصطلاح . لأن الكاهن يخبر عن الغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since Muslim scholars identify the father as the messenger Shuʿayb, they treat his conduct as revealed prior law, applicable unless abrogated, and derive several rulings from it.
rows.anchor: وللجزم بأنه شعيب الرسول جعل علماؤنا ما صدر منه في هذه القصة شرعا سابقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The precedent supports women working for a livelihood, required modesty, paternal guardianship in marriage, physical work as a dower, combining marriage and hire in one contract, and the lawfulness of hiring; al-Qurṭubī discusses these fully.
rows.anchor: ومنها مباشرة المرأة الأعمال والسعي في طرق المعيشة ، ووجوب استحيائها ، وولاية الأب في النكاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The father’s permission shows a woman may manage her property and appear publicly while covering what must be covered, if prior law is reported without abrogation; public reserve varies with custom and society.
rows.anchor: وفي إذنه لابنتيه بالسقي دليل على جواز معالجة المرأة أمور مالها وظهورها في مجامع الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition ʿalā is one of the forms used to state a contractual condition.
rows.anchor: حرف { على } من صيغ الشرط في العقود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾjurnī means to work for someone as a hired employee.
rows.anchor: و { تأجرني } مضارع آجره مثل نصره إذا كان أجيرا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥijaj is the plural of ḥijja, a year; its name derives from pilgrimage, which occurs yearly near the end of the Arabic calendar year.
rows.anchor: والحجج : اسم جمع حجة بكسر الحاء وهي السنة ، مشتقة من اسم الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The father proposes making marriage conditional on a hire contract; the proposal itself is neither a marriage nor a hire until Moses agrees, and it supports joining the two contracts.
rows.anchor: والتزام جعل تزويجه مشروطا بعقد الإجارة بينهما عرض منه على موسى وليس بعقد نكاح

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report tells of a woman who offered herself to the Prophet; he did not marry her but married her to a man present who lacked a dower, in exchange for teaching her what he knew of the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: حديث المرأة التي عرضت نفسها على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فلم يتزوجها وزوجها من رجل

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: The well-known Mālikī position voids a marriage condition that conflicts with marriage, annulling before consummation or confirming it afterward with the standard dower; a compatible condition is canceled without annulling the marriage.
rows.anchor: والمشهور من مذهب مالك أن الشرط المقارن لعقد النكاح إن كان مما ينافي عقد النكاح فهو باطل

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Another report from Mālik is that all conditions are initially disliked, but if made, they stand.
rows.anchor: وعن مالك أيضا : تكره الشروط كلها ابتداء فإن وقع مضى

rows.speaker: أشهب وأصبغ
rows.claim: Ashhab and Aṣbagh allow the condition; Abū Bakr ibn al-ʿArabī selects their view, which Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers based on this verse and the Prophetic command to honor conditions made in marriage.
rows.anchor: وقال أشهب وأصبغ : الشرط جائز واختاره أبو بكر بن العربي وهو الحق للآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense makes the hire the daughter’s dower; alternatively, it may require only the hire, with the dower governed by their own law, since legal definitions can differ across revealed laws.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الآية أيضا أن الإجارة المذكورة جعلت مهرا للبنت . ويحتمل أن المشروط التزام الإجارة لا غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the apparent reading is right, the dower was the benefit of Moses’s work for Shuʿayb; the daughter may have consented by hearing and remaining silent under their custom, or the father may have been entitled to the dower under their law.
rows.anchor: وإذا أخذنا بظاهر الآية كانت دالة على أنهما جعلا المهر منافع إجارة الزوج لشعيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the verse is ambiguous, it cannot alone prove that a woman’s dower may be her husband’s hired services; the issue should be tested against legal principles and the general meaning of dower, which can include valuable services.
rows.anchor: وإذ قد كان في الآية إجمال لم تكن كافية في الاحتجاج على جواز جعل مهر المرأة منافع من إجارة زوجها
